## Why it made the list

Imagine sipping your morning coffee on the engawa (wooden veranda), the Sea of Japan spread out below you, in a proper old kominka for under $60k. This one sits high on a hillside in Maizuru, up on the Kyoto coast, a couple hours from Kyoto city itself.

## Is €54,280 a good price for this home?

19 of the 35 homes in Japan on RealHunt have a lower asking price.

Asking prices are what the seller asks, not what homes sell for. Compare with recent sales in the same village before you make an offer.

## What it costs to buy this home

Buying in Japan adds about 6-9% in taxes and fees on top of the price: roughly €3,257 to €4,885 here, so plan for about €57,537 to €59,165 in total.

The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

Every year: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

General information, not tax advice: ask a local lawyer or notary for the exact figure.

## Where it is: Maizuru

The home is in Maizuru, Kyoto, Japan.

The nearest airport is about 54 km away (Konotori Tajima Airport (TJH)); the nearest shop is about 1 km away; the nearest train station is about 1 km away (東舞鶴). Distances are in a straight line.
